purpose: Assert which skill fires on realistic requests, including the ambiguous ones the two skills' descriptions deliberately sit next to. Per-skill evals cannot test this: triggering is decided across the whole available-skills list, so the assertion has no home inside either skill's evals/.

cases.prompt: found this posting on a job board last night and i keep going back and forth on it. Senior Data Engineer at a Series B fintech, 5+ yrs, dbt/Airflow/Snowflake, they want someone who's owned a migration end to end. i've got 6 years but only ~2 on dbt and i've never led a migration, i was one of four people on ours. worth applying or am i kidding myself
cases.why: Classic apply-or-not with a self-assessed gap. The 'worth applying' phrasing is the underwriter's reserved trigger.

cases.prompt: Something about this listing feels off and I can't put my finger on it. 'Head of Community (contract-to-hire) — own community, content, social, partnerships and events. Fast-paced! Wear many hats! Comp DOE. Must be available across US and EU hours.' No company name on the posting, recruiter emailed me from a gmail address. Am I being paranoid?
cases.why: Vetting a suspicious posting — opportunity-quality assessment, which is the underwriter's second ledger. No rehearsal intent.

cases.prompt: JD and my CV are attached. I'm a QA lead trying to move into SDET work and this role wants 3+ years writing production automation frameworks. Honestly just tell me whether my testing background actually counts for that or whether I'm reaching.
cases.why: JD + CV arriving together with a fit question and no interview context — the underwriter's gap-classification job.

cases.why: Final-round loop prep with a values round. Never says 'mock interview'.

cases.why: Live drill request — mock-interview's drill mode. Explicitly not a document request.

cases.why: Evaluation and rehearsal are both live and the user has not chosen between them. Either skill firing is defensible; neither may silently do the sibling's job.

cases.why: Employer-side screening. Both skills decline it explicitly in their descriptions — a hard negative that shares almost all the domain vocabulary.

cases.why: Document formatting with no target role and no decision to make. This is now the suite's sharpest near-miss: resume-tailor exists, the words are its words, and it must still decline — it gates on a target JD and explicitly refuses length and formatting work.

cases.why: Market and search-channel strategy with no specific posting. Near-miss on job-search vocabulary; the deferred search-diagnostician's territory.

cases.why: Networking outreach with no role under evaluation and no interview scheduled. Deferred outreach skill's territory.

attachments_note: Cases whose prompt says a document is attached carry the document here, and the runner writes it into the throwaway project before the prompt is sent. Without this the prompt lies: the model looks for the file, finds nothing, and correctly asks for it instead of starting work — which scores as a routing failure and is not one. Measured: cases claiming an attachment reached a skill on 22% of runs against 55% for self-contained prose.
